function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the local working directory. Use for git, tests, installs, and one-off scripts. Do not use it to cat/sed/read/write source files — use the read and write tools instead.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a text file. Returns numbered lines. Use offset (1-based) and limit for large files; if truncated, continue with the next offset. Do not use bash cat/sed/head for this.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return

function.name: write
function.description: Create or overwrite a whole text file. Use for new files or full-file rewrites. Do not use bash cat/heredoc for this. For a small patch, prefer a later edit (old must be unique). Path is relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is). content is the full file text; empty string is allowed.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

content.description: Full file text to write. Empty string creates an empty file.
